historical_reviews.deepseek: A Samsung-only filter and first-controller path can silently omit valid platform disks and cannot prove the endpoint-to-disk association demanded by the SPEC.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly restores full `lspci -nn`, per-approved-BDF verbose link context and controller identity while excluding reset/rescan operations.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: The bandwidth result must be derived from actual negotiated generation and width for the exact endpoint, not inferred from vendor ID or maximum capability. Every expected BDF needs a stable correlation to controller model/serial because bridges, retimers and multiple endpoints may share a vendor family.

original_test_intent: Verify every in-scope NVMe disk endpoint's PCI vendor/device identity and actual negotiated link speed, lane width and effective bandwidth against the approved SPEC.
original_method: Authenticate the SUT, enumerate the complete PCI tree with numeric IDs, map each expected storage controller and physical disk to its exact BDF, capture unfiltered verbose configuration including LnkCap/LnkSta and error status, correlate controller model/serial read-only, then compare IDs and normalized link bandwidth with a versioned recipe.
manual_activity: The storage/PCIe owner approves the complete endpoint-to-disk map, expected vendor/device IDs, negotiated generation/width and mismatch disposition.
required_inputs: Expected vendor and device IDs per endpoint
Verified host-key SSH with secret-safe authentication
safety_requirements: Use read-only PCI configuration and NVMe identify queries
Do not filter the initial inventory to one vendor
Do not assume `/dev/nvme0` is the intended disk
Never expose credentials or disable host authenticity
Do not reset, remove, rescan or retrain PCIe devices
Do not write, format or sanitize NVMe media
Preserve complete raw output and exit status
agent_execution_scope: Verify host, tools and approved topology
Capture verbose configuration for every approved endpoint
Collect read-only controller identity for disk correlation
Parse vendor/device, LnkCap, LnkSta and error status
Compare normalized fields and report without mutation or verdict
engineer_actions: Approve every disk/BDF mapping and expected ID
Explain optional or alternate vendor endpoints
Resolve downtraining, link-error or identity discrepancies

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lspci -vv -d 144d:` narrows coverage to one vendor and does not preserve the source's complete numeric ID inventory; `/dev/nvme0` is volatile and the nested quoting can break the identify filter. Unsafe SSH further invalidates provenance.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: With verified SSH, capture complete `lspci -nn`, then `lspci -s <approved-BDF> -nn -vvv` and read-only controller identity for each mapped disk; compare actual LnkSta generation/width and numeric IDs to the SPEC.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Every disk endpoint, vendor/device ID, speed, bandwidth and the 10-minute estimate remain in scope.

modernized_recommendation.status: COMPLETE DISK-ENDPOINT IDENTITY AND NEGOTIATED-LINK MATRIX
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Key evidence by approved BDF and controller serial, retaining numeric IDs, topology path, LnkCap, LnkSta, link-error context and calculated actual bandwidth for every disk.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Eliminates hardcoded vendor/device-node assumptions and adds complete endpoint correlation and actual-bandwidth normalization.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A vendor-filtered query can pass while an expected non-Samsung disk is absent, and controller model output can pass while the corresponding PCIe link is downtrained.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Queries are read-only, but topology ambiguity can produce a false pass; link speed alone does not establish usable storage performance and this case does not perform I/O benchmarking.

project_override_considerations: Supply the canonical BDF map after any bifurcation/riser/BIOS changes, allowed alternate vendor/device IDs, target LnkSta values, whether LnkCap is informational, and the formula/units used for bandwidth acceptance.
expected_evidence: SUT/BIOS/topology identity, approved disk/controller/BDF map and SPEC revision
Verified SSH provenance, pciutils/nvme-cli versions and timestamps
Complete raw `lspci -nn` plus per-BDF `-nn -vvv` and controller identity outputs
Per-endpoint vendor/device ID, LnkCap/LnkSta, calculated bandwidth and error-context comparison
Optional/missing/downtrained disposition, preserved logs, no-mutation audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define a read-only PCIe identity and link comparison for disks. DeepSeek's hardcoded narrowing is not source authority.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The check is technically clear; the owner-supplied map, SPEC and secure tools are finite prerequisites, so classification is REQUIRES.

review_improvement: Prevents one vendor and one volatile device node from standing in for complete PCIe disk coverage, and makes negotiated bandwidth independently auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: PCI numeric IDs establish endpoint type but do not establish physical disk identity, while an NVMe character-device index can change across boots. Binding controller serial to BDF closes that identity gap. Link acceptance then must use `LnkSta`, since a Gen5 x4-capable endpoint operating at Gen4 x2 still reports the desired maximum in `LnkCap` but provides materially less bandwidth.
